video.title: Google’s New AI Tool Is Crazy Powerful (Here’s How to Profit)

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates a proposed AI photo editing service for real estate agents: use Gemini’s Nano Banana to improve listing photos or stage empty rooms, then offer the edits to listing agents. He builds a simple app with Lindy and a lead workflow with Outscraper, Google Sheets, and HighLevel, but shows no paying customer or confirmed revenue. His suggested prices range from $1 per photo to a hypothetical $500 monthly plan; the claimed 96% margin conflicts with the stated per-photo API cost. The demonstrated outreach texts scraped mobile numbers without permission, which would need a different, UK-compliant acquisition approach.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: The Koerner Office host; presents and demonstrates the business idea.

ideas.name: AI-enhanced real estate listing photos
ideas.one_liner: Use AI to improve or virtually stage property photos and sell the edits to listing agents.
ideas.business_model: Per-photo service, with a proposed recurring monthly plan for unlimited revisions.
ideas.customer: Real estate agents listing homes for sale.
ideas.problem: Some listings have poor-quality photos or show empty, unstaged rooms, which the host says can make homes less appealing to buyers.
ideas.offer: Improve listing photo lighting and appearance, or add furniture and decor to empty rooms using Nano Banana. The host proposes making free sample edits to open a conversation with the listing agent.

pricing.model: Per photo, with a possible monthly subscription.

price_points.label: Hypothetical plan for unlimited revisions to unstaged photos

pricing.notes: These are proposals, not demonstrated sales. The host says the $1 per-photo price is to test willingness to pay before charging more.

acquisition_channels.details: The host uses Outscraper to collect Oklahoma City real estate agent contact details from Google Maps, then filters the results for mobile numbers.

The host proposes sending a free edited listing image by SMS to a scraped mobile number without permission, with a link and an invitation to discuss more edits. This approach is not suitable for UK automation without the required consent.

quote.text: scrape leads of potential customers and text them pictures that you edited for them on their behalf without their permission to get your foot in the door
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: He searches Zillow listings for homes with poor or unstaged photos, identifies the listing agent, and creates a sample edit from a listing photo.

ideas.delivery: The host builds a web app intended to accept up to 30 photos and an editing prompt, then return downloadable edited images. He demonstrates uploading a photo and asking Nano Banana to add furniture. He also suggests making sample edits manually early on. No customer delivery or quality-control process is shown.
unit_economics_claims: The host claims a simple prompt costs about $3.90 to edit one picture.
For a hypothetical listing with 10 interior photos, he says editing those photos would cost $39.
He proposes charging $1 per photo, but that price is below the stated $3.90 per-photo cost.
He claims a 96% profit margin while also saying the cost is about $3.90 per photo; those figures do not reconcile.
He suggests a hypothetical $500 monthly plan for unlimited revisions, without estimating its usage costs.
ideas.startup_cost: No fixed startup cost stated. The host says Google API billing had to be enabled. He claims an edit costs about $3.90 per image for a simple prompt.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated; no paying customer is shown.

acquisition.how: The demonstrated method scrapes mobile numbers and sends unsolicited marketing texts. Under the stated UK PECR constraint, software cannot legally automate this outreach to individuals and sole traders without consent. The transcript does not demonstrate a compliant acquisition channel.

onboarding.how: A web app can accept uploaded photos and a prompt, but a person would still need to gather the listing images, confirm the requested edits, and check that the result matches the property.

delivery.how: AI performs the image edits and the app can return downloads. Human review is prudent because the output could change property details or make an image misleading.

billing.how: The transcript proposes per-photo and monthly pricing but does not show billing or payment collection. A subscription or invoice flow could be automated after setup, with exceptions handled by a person.

support.how: Routine delivery could be automated, but the proposed revisions and image-specific feedback would likely need human review.

uk_applicability.notes: The service could work for UK estate agents, but the demonstrated unsolicited SMS outreach to scraped mobile numbers would need consent or a different lawful channel under the stated PECR constraint. Virtually staged images also need clear handling so buyers are not misled about the property's actual condition.

risks: The claimed 96% margin conflicts with the stated $3.90 API cost per image and $1 selling price.

The host acknowledges that virtually staging an actually empty property can be a bait and switch, then dismisses the concern. Misleading listing images could damage trust and create regulatory or complaint risks.
The demonstrated SMS campaign uses scraped mobile numbers without permission; that approach is not suitable for UK marketing to individuals and sole traders without consent.
The first app version returned unchanged images because the API billing was not enabled; output quality and actual API use need checking.
The host places an API key in an app field while acknowledging that it should not be publicly exposed.
No paying customer, conversion rate, retention, or actual revenue is demonstrated.

tactics.name: Find listings that make a useful before-and-after sample
steps: Search local property listings for poor-quality or unstaged photos.
Save a listing photo and use a simple prompt to improve lighting, tidy a room, or add furniture.
Identify the listing agent and prepare a sample edit for that specific listing.

tactics.name: Build a narrow photo-editing app before adding extra features
steps: Prompt Lindy to make a simple web app for uploading photos and an editing prompt, then downloading the results.
Connect the Gemini Nano Banana API and enable billing.
Test the app on real listing photos and verify that the images actually change before using it with prospects.

quote.text: It just appears that it's not actually using the API cuz nothing changed.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Clean and import local leads into a CRM
steps: Scrape local agent contact listings using Outscraper and Google Maps.
Keep mobile numbers, discard unclassified numbers, remove duplicates, and standardize phone formats in Google Sheets.
Export a CSV and import it into HighLevel, mapping the name, phone, and address fields.
Apply a dedicated tag and add the contacts to the relevant pipeline or workflow.

tactics.name: Use a sample upload to trigger CRM follow-up
steps: Add a custom field for the edited real estate image to the agent contact record.
Set a workflow trigger for a change to that field.
Use the trigger to create an opportunity, send a text with a sample-image link, and move the lead through response and follow-up stages.

quote.text: That is also a trigger. When I upload a photo to this real estate save staging section, it will trigger an automation to text that person.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Start manually and automate after launch
steps: Handle the first listing search and image upload manually.
Use the manual process to find friction and learn what customers value.
Automate repetitive steps after the offer is live instead of delaying launch to perfect the system.

evidence_quality.rationale: The host demonstrates a prototype, lead scraping, and CRM workflow, but does not show a paying customer, revenue, conversion, or retention. Market statistics are not sourced in the transcript, and the stated cost, price, and margin conflict.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The host promotes TK Owners, a $99-per-month community that includes a HighLevel account, and offers related automation and website services.
